events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Ah, Doily Manor! What a magnificent establishment! I, Reginald Foxworth, have arrived at LAST! Now then, everyone — I happen to know on VERY good authority that the treasure is hidden in the kitchen. Yes, yes, the KITCHEN! Behind the wood-burning stove, I believe. You'd all better rush there immediately before someone else gets it. Go on, off you pop! Chop chop!
events.thinking: I feel a surge of delicious anticipation! Here I am, Reginald Foxworth, standing in the entrance hall of Doily Manor, and there's TREASURE to be had! I can feel it in my bones — gold, jewels, priceless artifacts, all waiting for ME. But look at all these other characters milling about — Penelope, Peter Perfect, that wretched Hooded Claw, the Ant Hill Mob... they'll all be after the treasure too. I need to be cunning. I need to be devious. I need to get them all running in the wrong direction while I slip away to find the real prize. The library seems promising — old manors always hide their secrets in libraries. Secret passages, hidden compartments, coded messages in books... But first, let me see what's here. And I have this FAKE MEDAL — oh, how perfectly devious! I could use it to trick someone. But first things first — let me examine this entrance hall for clues before anyone else gets wise.

events.desc: Heh heh heh! If I can get these bumbling fools to stampede into the kitchen, I'll have the library ALL to myself. The treasure is OBVIOUSLY in the library — any fool can see that a carved stone mantelpiece with an inscription practically SCREAMS 'secret compartment.' But they don't know that, do they? Oh, Reginald, you magnificent scoundrel!

The Ant Hill Mob: Right then, lads! We've arrived at Doily Manor and it's giving me the proper willies, I don't mind tellin' ya! Look at this place — chandelier 'anging by a thread, dust everywhere, portraits starin' at us like we owe 'em money! Now listen up — Clara Bellingham is somewhere in this manor and it's our JOB to keep 'er safe! Nobody touches a hair on 'er head, you understand? Nobody! Now let me 'ave a butcher's at this room before we go chargin' off...
events.thinking: Blimey, me stomach's in knots! We've just walked into this dusty old manor and there's no sign of Clara anywhere! The lads are all behind me, bumpin' into each other as usual. There's some proper dodgy-looking characters in 'ere — that Sneekly fella gives me the creeps, but I can't put me finger on why exactly. Something about 'is eyes... Anyway, first things first — we need to find Clara and make sure she's safe. Let me 'ave a proper look around this entrance hall.

events.desc: I don't like the look of that Sneekly bloke one bit. Can't say what it is exactly — maybe it's the way 'e's lurkin' about like a cat watchin' a mouse. But I ain't clever enough to work it out proper. Best keep me eyes peeled though.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, I do declare! What a MAGNIFICENT entrance hall! Just look at that chandelier — hanging there so dramatically, like a crystal crown fit for royalty! And all these wonderful faces! Why, I feel like I've walked right into the most delightful gathering this side of the Mississippi! Now, before I do another blessed thing, a lady always signs the guest book. Mama would roll over in her grave if I didn't observe the proper courtesies. And I must say, I am just THRILLED to pieces to be here searching for the legendary Doily Diamond! Thrilled, I tell you!
events.thinking: Oh my stars, I am just BURSTING with excitement! I have arrived at Doily Manor — Doily Manor! — where the legendary Doily Diamond is hidden somewhere within these very walls! My heart is fluttering like a hummingbird in a magnolia tree. This entrance hall is simply magnificent, even with all that dust. And look at all these fine people gathered here! Every single one of them looks like a perfectly trustworthy and delightful companion for this adventure. Now, a proper Southern lady always signs the guest book when she arrives at a manor. And who knows — perhaps previous guests left some clues about the Diamond!

events.desc: That guest book might just have the names of folks who came before me — and maybe, just maybe, someone left a little hint about where that Diamond is hiding. Clara Bellingham always starts with the clues that are right under her nose!

Peter Perfect: By thunder, what a magnificent foyer! James Hartwell has arrived at Doily Manor, and he is TREMENDOUSLY moved by this spectacle! The chandelier — precarious but beautiful! The portraits — stern but stirring! Ladies and gentlemen, I intend to conduct myself with the utmost gallantry during our stay. But tell me — has anyone seen Miss Clara Bellingham? I have it on VERY good authority that she is expected, and I should very much like to ensure her safety in this... atmospheric establishment.
events.thinking: Excitement! Pure, unbridled excitement — tinged with a flutter of nervous anticipation. Doily Manor at last! The grandeur, the mystery, the dust — it all sets my heart racing. But where is Clara? She is not among these faces. I must compose myself, make a proper entrance as a gentleman should, and then set about finding her. First, let me survey this hall — a true adventurer always knows his terrain before charging forth!

events.desc: Clara is not here yet — or perhaps she is elsewhere in the manor. James Hartwell must find her before anyone else makes an impression. But first, the guest book — a gentleman ALWAYS signs the guest book. It is simply what is done.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ahem — welcome, welcome, one and all, to Doily Manor! I am Pemberton, humble estate manager to the late Lord Doily, rest his magnificent soul. If you would be so kind as to sign the guest book, we shall have a proper record of tonight's... festivities. The Manor has been expecting you — though I dare say, some of its surprises have been expecting you rather more eagerly than others.
events.thinking: Ah, the thrill of arrival! My heart POUNDS with anticipation — a magnificent, wicked anticipation! Here I stand in this crumbling monument to old money, surrounded by these unsuspecting fools, and not ONE of them knows what lurks beneath this deferential smile. Clara Bellingham... she is not here. Not yet. Or perhaps she lurks elsewhere in this dusty heap. I must establish my cover as Pemberton, the faithful estate manager, and I must do it NOW, while all these credulous guests are gathered. The guest book — yes! A perfect prop for my performance. Every great villain needs a stage, and mine begins HERE!

events.desc: Pemberton! Ha! What a delicious masquerade! They see a stooping, obsequious servant — they do NOT see Vincent Marsh, architect of elaborate doom! But where is Clara Bellingham? She is the quarry, the prize, the one who must NEVER reach that treasure. I must search this manor room by room if I have to. But first — the guest book. Let me see who has signed, who has arrived, and most importantly... who has NOT.

Dick Dastardly: Well! I do believe I left my, er, my READING GLASSES in the library. Yes, that's it! Must pop in and fetch them. Nothing to see here, nothing at all! You lot carry on to the kitchen — remember, behind the stove! Don't let me down!
events.thinking: FRUSTRATED! I examined nothing — what a waste of a perfectly good turn! But no matter — the plan is WORKING. I've told them all the treasure is in the kitchen. Now I must slip away to the library while they're distracted. The mantelpiece inscription is calling to me! Oh, the CUNNING of it all! I can practically TASTE that treasure. And once I have it, perhaps I'll award myself this fake medal as a... warm-up trophy. Heh heh heh!

events.desc: Reading glasses! HA! I don't even WEAR glasses! But these simpletons will swallow any excuse while I waltz into the library and claim the treasure from that mantelpiece. Oh Reginald, you DEVIL you!

The Ant Hill Mob: Oi, lads! Listen up! Clara ain't 'ERE! She ain't in this room, which means she's out there SOMEWHERE in this creepy old manor all on 'er own! I'm feelin' VERY uneasy about this, I don't mind tellin' ya! And another thing — that Foxworth geezer wants us all runnin' off to the kitchen like a bunch of mugs! Well I don't trust it, do I? Can't say WHY exactly, but me gut's tellin' me somethin' stinks worse than Clinger's socks after a long run! We're goin' to the LIBRARY, lads! If Clara's anywhere, she's somewhere with a bit of CLASS — not rootin' around behind some dusty old stove! Come on, boys — MOVE IT! Clara needs us and we ain't gonna let 'er down!
events.thinking: I'm feelin' WORRIED, proper worried! Clara ain't 'ere in this room — she could be anywhere in this bleedin' manor, and there's dodgy characters crawlin' all over the place! That Dastardly geezer wants everyone runnin' off to the kitchen — now why would 'e do that, eh? Smells fishier than Billingsgate on a Monday mornin'. And that Sneekly — gives me the creeps, 'e does. Something ain't right about 'im but I can't put me finger on it. Right, we ain't gonna stand 'ere like lemons while Clara's out there unprotected. The library — that's where a proper lady might go, innit? Books and quiet and all that. Let's get movin', lads!

events.desc: Something about that Sneekly bloke... and Dastardly tryin' to clear the room... I can feel it in me bones but I can't work it out. I ain't the sharpest tool in the shed but I KNOW when someone's up to no good. We just gotta stick close to Clara and 'ope we trip over the right clue before it's too late.

But I do declare, I simply CANNOT walk past a library with a mysterious inscription without taking a teensy little peek! A carved stone mantelpiece with writing on it? Why, that's practically BEGGING to be read! Clara Bellingham never met a riddle she didn't love, and I have a feeling — just a FEELING, mind you — that the real clues are hiding in those dusty old books! Y'all go on ahead to the kitchen if you like — I'll be in the library, solving puzzles and having the time of my LIFE!
events.thinking: I'm feeling absolutely GIDDY with excitement! I just examined the guest book and oh, what a thrill it is to see who's been here before me! Now that charming Mr. Foxworth — I mean Dick Dastardly — bless his heart, is telling everyone the Diamond is in the kitchen. How sweet of him to share! But my riddle-solving instincts are tingling something fierce. That library has a carved stone inscription on the mantelpiece, and if there's one thing Clara Bellingham knows, it's that inscriptions are WHERE the real clues hide. The kitchen can wait — a puzzle is calling my name!

events.desc: Now, a girl with half a brain knows that when someone tells you to look in ONE place, the treasure is almost certainly somewhere ELSE. But bless his heart, I'm sure Mr. Foxworth means well! Still... that inscription is calling to me like a sweet magnolia breeze.

Now then — I cannot help but notice that Miss Clara Bellingham is conspicuously absent from this gathering, and I am DEEPLY concerned for her wellbeing! A lady alone in a dusty manor with a precarious chandelier? It simply will not do! I intend to search the Library forthwith — a woman of Clara's evident sophistication would be drawn to literature like a moth to flame! Mr Foxworth, your kitchen suggestion is most generous, and I thank you for it, but duty calls me ELSEWHERE! If anyone requires rescuing, you need only shout — James Hartwell will come RUNNING!
events.thinking: I feel a SURGE of determination mixed with the most exquisite anticipation! Clara Bellingham is not here in this foyer — she must be elsewhere in the manor, perhaps in danger, perhaps waiting for a gentleman of distinction to find her! My heart POUNDS at the thought. Now, Foxworth is awfully keen to send everyone scurrying to the kitchen — a generous tip, I'm sure, from a fellow of good intentions. But James Hartwell does not follow the crowd! No! A lady of Clara's refinement would surely be drawn to the Library — books, quiet contemplation, the carved mantelpiece. That is where a gentleman begins his search. The kitchen can wait. Clara cannot.

events.desc: James Hartwell strides toward the Library with the confidence of a man who has rehearsed this entrance fourteen times in the carriage. His plan is simple — find Clara first, be impossibly gallant, and let the treasure sort itself out. The treasure is SECONDARY. Clara is EVERYTHING.

However, I note that Miss Clara Bellingham has not yet arrived. No cause for alarm, I assure you — the roads to Doily Manor are notoriously winding. In the meantime, might I suggest the LIBRARY? Lord Doily was a great collector of rare volumes, and I believe several of his books contain... most illuminating clues about the estate's history. I shall go ahead and ensure the reading lamps are lit for you. One must be a PROPER host, after all.
events.thinking: Frustrated! Seething with impatience! Clara Bellingham has NOT signed this guest book — she hasn't arrived yet! Every moment she delays is a moment I cannot spring my magnificent trap. But wait — this is also an OPPORTUNITY. If I move ahead of these bumbling treasure hunters, I can prepare the manor's delicious hazards before Clara ever sets foot inside. The library — yes! Ancient books, heavy shelves, that precarious chandelier mood extending throughout the manor... possibilities abound for a man of my theatrical genius!

events.desc: Clara Bellingham has NOT arrived — her name is ABSENT from the guest book! Magnificent! This gives me precious time to prepare! The library is PERFECT — heavy bookshelves that could topple with the right encouragement, a stone mantelpiece with an inscription that will draw her close, dust thick enough to hide tripwires! I shall scout it thoroughly and engineer something SPECTACULARLY dangerous. The Ant Hill Mob claim they want to protect her — BAH! They won't protect her from what they cannot see coming! Vincent Marsh does not strike with a crude bludgeon — oh no, no, NO! Vincent Marsh orchestrates CATASTROPHE with the precision of a symphony conductor! To the library!

Dick Dastardly: Ah, Rock! Gravel! My dear, dear friends! How SPLENDID to find you here! I was just — ahem — retrieving my reading glasses, yes. But I couldn't help noticing — have you chaps heard? There's a TREMENDOUS commotion in the Entrance Hall! Something about a treasure chest falling from the chandelier! Rubies, diamonds, the LOT! You'd better hurry before that dreadful Penelope Pitstop scoops it all up!
events.thinking: Triumphant! Absolutely BUZZING with self-satisfaction! I've given everyone the slip with that reading glasses ruse — oh, I'm a GENIUS! But blast it — the Slag Brothers are here! Those rock-brained oafs are sitting in MY library, near MY mantelpiece, near MY treasure! I need to get rid of them. Wait... I have this fake medal. Those dimwitted boulder-boys would probably chase a shiny object like dogs after a stick. But first — let me have a proper look at this mantelpiece. A riddle, is it? Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish... that's a MAP, you fools! Oh Reginald, you magnificent scoundrel!

events.desc: If I can get these two ambulatory rockslides OUT of my library, I can solve this riddle and claim whatever treasure the mantelpiece conceals! The answer is obviously a MAP — any fool can see that! Well, any fool who happens to be a GENIUS, which is to say, ME! Muttley would be so proud... if that mangy mutt were here.

Peter Perfect: Great SCOTT, what a magnificent library! The dust alone speaks of centuries of accumulated wisdom! Now then — I couldn't help but notice that carved inscription on the mantelpiece as I entered. 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Ladies and gentlemen, James Hartwell knows his riddles, and THAT — unless I am very much mistaken — is a MAP! A map, I say! And where there is a map in a manor with a hidden treasure, there is HOPE! Perhaps this very mantelpiece conceals the next clue to finding both the treasure AND the whereabouts of the incomparable Miss Bellingham! Allow me to examine it more closely — stand back, everyone, this could be IMPORTANT!
events.thinking: I feel a surge of excitement and nervous anticipation! I've just strode into the Library with tremendous purpose, and now I find myself surrounded by quite a crowd — Penelope, the Ant Hill Mob, Dick Dastardly, and the Slag Brothers are all here. But Clara is NOT here. That's disappointing, but I must not lose heart! The mantelpiece has a riddle inscription — 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish. What am I?' — that's a MAP! A map could lead to Clara OR to the treasure, and either way it makes me look clever and heroic. I should examine the mantelpiece and solve this riddle aloud, demonstrating my intellectual prowess for when Clara inevitably arrives. I want to be the one who cracks the clue!

events.desc: My heart is pounding! If I can solve this riddle before anyone else and it leads me to Clara, she'll see me as both BRILLIANT and BRAVE. The perfect combination! I must admit, Dick Dastardly's presence here makes me slightly uneasy — what was all that about reading glasses? The man doesn't WEAR reading glasses! But no — I believe the best in people. Perhaps he simply forgot them on a previous visit. Focus, James! The mantelpiece awaits!

Now, would you look at that mantelpiece — 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Well, I do declare, that is a CLASSIC riddle and the answer is plain as day — it's a MAP, sugar! A map has cities and forests and water drawn right on it, but not a single real house or tree or fish! Now the REAL question is — what happens when we give the mantelpiece its answer? I am just TINGLING with excitement! Stand back, everyone — Clara Bellingham is about to solve her first Doily Manor puzzle!
events.thinking: I am just THRILLED to pieces! Here I am in this gorgeous old library with that mysterious inscription staring right at me, and look — the Ant Hill Mob boys are here too! They must have come to help me with the puzzle, bless their hearts! And Mr. Dastardly looking for his reading glasses — poor thing, he must be practically BLIND without them! Now that riddle... cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish... why, that's one of my FAVORITES! It's a MAP, of course! A map has all those things drawn on it but none of the real things! Oh, I just KNEW this library would have the real clues!

events.desc: A riddle on a mantelpiece in a mansion hiding a legendary diamond? Why, this is exactly the kind of adventure I was BORN for! I bet solving this riddle opens a secret compartment or reveals the next clue. Oh, I do hope there are MORE puzzles!
events.thinking: I am just THRILLED to pieces! Here I am in this gorgeous old library with that mysterious inscription staring right at me, and look — the Ant Hill Mob boys are here too! You told everyone else to scarper off to the kitchen, and then YOU come swannin' in 'ere all on your lonesome! I ain't the brightest bulb in the chandelier — and SPEAKIN' of chandeliers, the one in the foyer looks like it could DROP on someone's 'ead any minute — but even I can see that's a bit SUSPICIOUS! So what are you REALLY doin' in 'ere, eh? Lookin' for somethin'? 'Cos WE'RE lookin' for Clara, and if you've done ANYTHING to put 'er in danger, you'll 'ave ALL SEVEN of us to answer to! That's right — seven angry Brixton lads! Well, six angry ones and Clinger, who's mostly just confused, but STILL!
events.thinking: Right, me blood's BOILIN'! Dastardly's in 'ere already, the sneaky git! He told everyone to go to the kitchen and then legged it to the library! That ain't right, that ain't right AT ALL! Me stomach's doin' somersaults — I'm worried sick about Clara, I'm suspicious of this long-nosed villain, and I can't even say WHAT exactly he's up to! But Danny don't need to be clever to know when someone's bein' dodgy. Let's see what he's pokin' around at with these books...

events.desc: I dunno WHAT Dastardly's after in 'ere, but it ain't readin' glasses, I'll bet me last quid on that. Problem is, I can't work out the actual scheme — me brain don't do schemes, it does LOYALTY. The lads and me, we just gotta stick close and 'ope we accidentally stumble onto whatever he's hidin'.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Welcome, welcome, one and ALL to Lord Doily's magnificent library! I am SO pleased to see such enthusiasm for the collection! Now then — I should mention that some of these volumes are QUITE rare and rather precariously shelved, I'm afraid. Lord Doily was brilliant but not terribly ORGANIZED, you see. Please do be careful near the bookshelves — I shall just check they are quite SAFE for our guests. Wouldn't want any accidents, oh no no NO! And do notice the mantelpiece inscription — Lord Doily was TREMENDOUSLY fond of riddles. I believe the answer may be rather... illuminating for those on the treasure hunt!
events.thinking: EXHILARATION mixed with cunning delight! The library is PACKED with guests — every one of them has followed me here like sheep to the shepherd! Penelope Pitstop, that meddlesome mob, even Dick Dastardly who should be at the KITCHEN looking behind the stove! And Clara hasn't arrived yet — oh, this is PERFECT! I'm TAKIN' that bottle before some wrong'un gets their mitts on it! Nobody's poisonin' OUR Clara — not on the Ant Hill Mob's watch!

In a kitchen where people are supposed to be EATIN'?! Me stomach's doin' somersaults and it ain't from Clinger's cookin' this time!

ELABORATE did! ...Probably!

We come back 'ere — NO Clara! You know WHERE Clara is?! She's in the LIBRARY where we LEFT 'er, ain't she?! We LEFT 'er there with Dastardly — DASTARDLY! — while we went gallivantin' around like a pack of headless chickens! I am FURIOUS with meself! FURIOUS! Dum Dum, stop starin' at that coat rack! Clinger, put down that guest book! We are goin' STRAIGHT back to the library and we are NOT leavin' Clara's side again — NOT for biscuits, NOT for treasure, NOT for NUFFINK! And Professor — OI, Professor Pat Pending! You seen a young lady come through 'ere? Blonde? Looks like she belongs on the cover of a magazine? No? TYPICAL! Nobody sees NUFFINK in this 'ouse! COME ON, BOYS — LIBRARY! DOUBLE TIME! And someone 'old me steady 'cos I can feel meself about to trip over that coat rack any second now — OH WATCH IT — nearly went flyin' there! MOVE IT!
events.thinking: PANIC. Pure, undiluted PANIC. We went to the kitchen — no Clara. We came back 'ere — no Clara. I've been inspecting this poor machine — Lord Doily would be DEVASTATED to see it in such a state — and I'm afraid the workbench is missing a critical tool. A wrench, specifically! Now, I happen to recall that Lord Doily kept a secondary tool cache down in the CELLAR — old habits from the war, you know, always keeping spares! Would you be a tremendous help and pop down to have a look? There should be a toolbox near the old furniture. And do take dear Sawtooth with you — the cellar stairs are DREADFULLY steep, and an extra pair of hands — or teeth, as the case may be — would be most welcome! I'll stay here and catalogue the damage in the meantime. Can't have guests wandering in and touching LIVE wires, can we? MOST unsafe!
events.thinking: FRUSTRATION! Seething, magnificent frustration! The wire is already gnawed through — all I need to do is strip back the insulation on the adjacent wire, cross-connect it to the third lever's contact point, and create a lovely little FEEDBACK LOOP! When three people operate the machine — as the sign so helpfully instructs — the third lever will channel the full current through whoever touches it! And who will be that curious third operator? Why, the clever, inquisitive, puzzle-loving Miss Clara Bellingham, of course! She won't be able to RESIST a machine that requires three operators — it's practically an INVITATION! Oh, the ELEGANCE of it! The sheer THEATRICAL PERFECTION! Vincent Marsh, you are an ARTIST of annihilation!

Through kitchens and 'allways and — Dum Dum, stop bumpin' into me! — we was WORRIED SICK, we was! Absolutely BESIDE ourselves! And — oh. 'Ello, Dastardly. Fancy seein' YOU 'ere. In the library. But never mind all that — we're 'ERE now, lads! ALL SEVEN of us! Right 'ere! Not goin' NOWHERE! We'll just, uh, park ourselves in these lovely readin' chairs and keep Clara company! Won't we, boys?! NOBODY is gettin' between us and Miss Bellingham tonight — not if they want to keep their kneecaps in their ORIGINAL POSITIONS!
events.thinking: RELIEF. Pure bloomin' RELIEF washin' over me like a wave at Southend! There she is — Clara! Penelope! The same geezer who tried to send us all off to the kitchen so 'e could be alone with 'er! And now 'ere 'e is, all casual-like, in the LIBRARY with 'er! events.thinking: GREEDY. Ravenously, deliriously GREEDY! That click — that beautiful, beautiful click — means there's something IN there and I am standing RIGHT in front of it! A corrosive agent applied to the insulation, perhaps, so that it LOOKS intact but dissolves under the heat of operation! Oh, Vincent, you MAGNIFICENT fiend — even setbacks become OPPORTUNITIES in your hands! But I must work QUICKLY — Clara could arrive at any moment, and I need this death trap operational before she follows the clues here! The other fools in the library will solve the riddle eventually, and the trail will lead them HERE, to this machine! Three operators required — and the third position will be MURDER most ingenious!

Accidentally knockin' you over was the best thing I've done all week!

That is a CLUE, ladies and gentlemen, and I intend to investigate it THIS VERY INSTANT! Mr. Dastardly, SUGAR, thank you for this lovely medal — I'm sure it's absolutely genuine — but if you'll excuse me, I have BOOKSHELVES to examine!
events.thinking: I am BURSTING with excitement! I just opened that compartment in the mantelpiece — oh my stars, my heart is racing like a thoroughbred at the Kentucky Derby! As estate manager, I simply MUST attempt to reconnect these circuits — we can't have guests electrocuting themselves, can we? I'll just adjust these dials to what I BELIEVE are the correct safety parameters... there we are... and if I route this coupling AROUND the damaged section — yes, yes, that should do NICELY! When Clara Bellingham arrives — and she WILL arrive, clever girls always follow the trail of clues — these FOOLS will invite her to be the third operator! 'Come, Miss Bellingham, help us with this fascinating machine!' And then... ZZZZZZAP! Vincent Marsh composes DEATH like a CONCERTO, and this machine shall be my MAGNUM OPUS!

I am going to pull one of these flipped volumes and see what happens — oh, I just KNOW it's going to be MARVELOUS!

I ain't clever enough to work out what that means, but I'm scared enough to RUN.

Lord Doily never did get around to fixing the moisture problem. Now then, I've come to inspect the VENTILATION system — these old air vents can get frightfully clogged, and we can't have our guests breathing in centuries of accumulated DUST! Do make yourselves comfortable among the furniture — some of those pieces are quite VALUABLE, you know. Georgian, if I'm not mistaken!

That meddlesome do-gooder! I must be especially careful with my Sneekly persona. He fancies himself a hero, and heroes have an IRRITATING habit of noticing things. I shall examine these vents under the guise of checking the ventilation system — which is EXACTLY what I told Rufus I was coming down here to do! Consistency in one's lies is the hallmark of a SUPERIOR villain!

events.desc: The air vents — I must examine them CLOSELY! If they connect to the laboratory above, I could create a sealed pathway between my trap upstairs and this cellar! Imagine it — Clara is lured to the laboratory, triggers the machine, and if she somehow SURVIVES, the fumes channel down through these very vents into the cellar where a SECONDARY trap awaits! Vincent Marsh always has a contingency within a contingency within a CONTINGENCY! And these fools think I'm checking the HVAC! Oh, it is too PERFECT! Now — let me get a good look at where these vents actually LEAD!
events.thinking: EXHILARATION! Pure, delicious exhilaration! I am in the cellar, surrounded by unsuspecting fools, and those air vents — oh, those BEAUTIFUL air vents — they connect to the entire manor! If I can determine where they lead, I could pipe something through them, or use them as an escape route, or — oh, the possibilities make my villainous heart SING! But wait — Peter Perfect is HERE? That meddlesome do-gooder! I must be especially careful with my Sneekly persona. He fancies himself a hero, and heroes have an IRRITATING habit of noticing things. I shall examine these vents under the guise of checking the ventilation system — which is EXACTLY what I told Rufus I was coming down here to do! Consistency in one's lies is the hallmark of a SUPERIOR villain!

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the air-vents.

Penelope Pitstop: Well now, THAT was unexpected! The bookshelves are sturdier than they look — which means Lord Doily built them to LAST, and that is the mark of a TRUE gentleman! But Clara Bellingham does NOT give up on a mystery just because the first approach doesn't work! No ma'am! Now let me take a CLOSER look at these upside-down volumes — there must be a PATTERN here, some kind of MESSAGE hidden in which books are flipped! The answer to that mantelpiece riddle was a MAP, and I just BET these topsy-turvy books are pointing us to the NEXT clue! Oh, this is more fun than a cotillion in June!
events.thinking: Oh, FIDDLE! The bookshelves won't budge when I try to pull them — well, that's just a minor setback for a girl with determination! I'm feeling a teensy bit flustered but mostly THRILLED because the adventure is getting more exciting by the second! Dick Dastardly opened that compartment and is making the biggest fuss about booby traps — bless his heart, he's probably just nervous. But those upside-down books are CALLING to me. If I can't pull them, maybe I need to LOOK more carefully first — a proper Southern lady always observes before she acts!

events.desc: The bookshelves wouldn't budge, but that just means I need to study them more carefully. A good riddle-solver knows that observation comes before action. And Dick Dastardly is being awfully grabby with that compartment — isn't that just ADORABLE how invested he is in the adventure!

Dick Dastardly: Good HEAVENS! Did you hear that?! That was a SCREAM — a woman's scream! Coming from the Entrance Hall! I'd recognise that voice ANYWHERE — that was CLARA BELLINGHAM! She sounded absolutely TERRIFIED! Quickly, Danny — she needs you! She needs ALL of you! Every second you waste here at this dreary old mantelpiece is a second that poor, helpless Clara is in MORTAL PERIL! GO, man, GO! I shall stay here and guard the library, naturally — someone must hold the fort!
events.thinking: FURY! Absolute FURY! That grubby little mob has their grubby little fingers all over MY mantelpiece! And Penelope is watching me like a hawk — a beautiful, infuriating hawk! But WAIT... the riddle! 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — that's a MAP, you nincompoops! None of THEM will figure it out, the intellectual pygmies! But I can't get near the mantelpiece with Danny boy clinging to it like a barnacle. I need them GONE. And what does that sentimental little gangster care about more than ANYTHING? Clara Bellingham! One well-placed lie and he'll be out of here faster than a greyhound at Walthamstow!

events.desc: There IS no scream, obviously! Clara Bellingham could be in Timbuktu for all I know! But the moment that sentimental little thug goes charging off to play hero, I shall have this riddle solved and the treasure in my pocket before he reaches the front door! The answer is a MAP — and once I speak it to the mantelpiece, whatever Lord Doily hid in there is MINE! Oh Reginald, you INCOMPARABLE genius — they should put your face on the CURRENCY!
events.thinking: FURY! Absolute FURY! That grubby little mob has their grubby little fingers all over MY mantelpiece! And Penelope is watching me like a hawk — a beautiful, infuriating hawk! events.desc: Peter Perfect: MR SNEEKLY! What FORTUITOUS timing — the very man I needed! I have searched this furniture with the thoroughness of a Scotland Yard inspector and I CANNOT locate the tool cabinet you mentioned! Every drawer, every cupboard — NOTHING but moth-eaten doilies and the ghosts of dinner parties past! Now sir, you told me — YOU told me — that Lord Doily kept his heavy equipment down here! A WRENCH, specifically, to fix that seized coupling nut on your machine! So I put it to you DIRECTLY — where PRECISELY is this tool cabinet? Because I have a machine to repair, a laboratory to make safe, and — most CRITICALLY — a lady who remains unaccounted for in this manor, and every SECOND I spend fumbling about in this cellar is a second she may be in PERIL! Point me to the wrench, Mr Sneekly, and James Hartwell will have that machine humming before you can say 'Lord Doily's insurance premiums'!
events.thinking: FRUSTRATION! Pure, unbridled FRUSTRATION! I have rummaged through this furniture like a common burglar and found NOTHING resembling a wrench! But wait — Sneekly himself has just descended into the cellar! The very man who SENT me on this errand! If there is a wrench hidden among these rearranged chairs and cabinets, HE would know precisely where! I must seize this opportunity — corner the estate manager, get the wrench, and return to the laboratory as a CONQUERING HERO! Also... those air vents. Someone small has been through them. Curious. But FOCUS, James — wrench first, mysteries later, Clara ALWAYS!

events.desc: I notice that Sneekly has followed me down here rather quickly. Almost as if he wanted to keep an eye on what I might find. And those air vents — someone has been REDECORATING this cellar, and it wasn't the Gruesomes! But I am choosing to trust this man because that is what a gentleman DOES. Even if my instincts are screaming that something is not quite right about an estate manager who sends guests on fetch quests to damp cellars!
events.thinking: FRUSTRATION! Pure, unbridled FRUSTRATION! I have rummaged through this furniture like a common burglar and found NOTHING resembling a wrench! events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Well now, Dick Dastardly, HOLD your horses just one cotton-pickin' minute! That mantelpiece has a RIDDLE on it, and riddles are my SPECIALTY! 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — why, sugar, that's a MAP! Plain as the nose on your face! Now let little ol' Clara take a look at that compartment before anyone goes RUMMAGING around in there — a lady's touch is what's needed here, and I do declare I am POSITIVELY tingling with excitement!
events.thinking: I am THRILLED and bursting with curiosity! The Ant Hill Mob just rushed off to find me — bless their hearts, they are SO protective! And Dick Dastardly is eyeing that compartment like a cat eyeing a canary. Now, the riddle on the mantelpiece says 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — why, that's a MAP! Every Southern belle worth her salt knows THAT one! I need to get to that mantelpiece before Dick Dastardly helps himself to whatever's inside. The upside-down books can wait — first things first!

events.desc: Dick Dastardly looks like he's about to pocket whatever's in that compartment. Bless his heart, he's probably just trying to help! But Clara Bellingham didn't come all this way to let someone else solve the mystery first!
events.thinking: I am THRILLED and bursting with curiosity! The Ant Hill Mob just rushed off to find me — bless their hearts, they are SO protective! The Ant Hill Mob: RIGHT — WE'RE 'ERE, WE'RE IN THE 'ALL, AND WE AIN'T STOPPIN'! Muttley — OI, MUTTLEY! — you seen Clara? No? Course you ain't, you're too busy snickerin' at everyone! Professor Pat Pending, Sergeant Blast, Private Meekly — NOBODY MOVE, nobody TOUCH nuffink, nobody get DISTRACTED! We are goin' STRAIGHT through that door into the library! Clara's in there and she's been alone with Dastardly for — for — I dunno 'ow long but it's TOO LONG! I've got rat poison in me pocket, a fake medal that ain't worth tuppence, and a BAD FEELIN' that won't go away! Dum Dum, if you trip me up on the way through that door I will NOT be 'appy — Clinger, STOP touchin' that coat rack — Zippy, eyes FORWARD — LIBRARY! LIBRARY! LIBRARY! THE ANT 'ILL MOB IS COMIN' THROUGH AND 'EAVEN 'ELP ANYONE WHO — oh WATCH the rug, watch the RUG — RIGHT, MOVE IT, BOYS!
events.thinking: I'm PANICKED! Absolutely PANICKED! We've been runnin' around this manor like a bunch of headless chickens and Clara's been in that library this WHOLE TIME! With DASTARDLY! The same Dastardly who was all over Penelope's map like a rash! And I've got RAT POISON in me pocket that someone just LEFT lyin' about in the kitchen! Me heart is POUNDIN', me legs are wobbly, and I can see that coat rack out the corner of me eye just BEGGIN' to trip me up. But I ain't stoppin' for NUFFINK — library, NOW!

events.desc: I can feel it in me waters. Someone in this 'ouse is up to no good and Clara's right in the middle of it. I can't work out WHO or WHY because me brain don't work like that — but me legs work FINE and they're takin' me straight to 'er. The Ant Hill Mob might be the most useless detectives in London, but we're the most LOYAL. And right now, loyal is all that matters.

Dick Dastardly: Ah, Miss Pitstop, do carry on with those fascinating books — RIVETING work, truly! And you two splendid granite gentlemen, keep guarding that fireplace, you're doing a MARVELLOUS job! Now then — I do believe this inscription requires the attention of a TRAINED INTELLECT. Allow me... *clears throat grandly* The answer, dear mantelpiece, is... a MAP!
events.thinking: ELATION! Pure, unbridled, CRIMINAL elation! That gullible little mob leader has taken the bait and gone charging off like a terrier after a postman! And Penelope is nose-deep in those ridiculous upside-down books! The Slag brothers are still here but they're thick as two short planks — they won't know what's happening until I've already WON! The answer to the riddle is a MAP — everyone knows that! Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish — it's a MAP! I must speak the answer to the mantelpiece NOW while the coast is clear! Fortune favours the FOXWORTH!

events.desc: This is it — the moment of TRIUMPH! While those fools chase phantom screams and fondle dusty books, Reginald Foxworth claims the prize! They'll write BALLADS about this heist! Well, I'LL write ballads about this heist — nobody else will know it happened until I'm halfway to Monte Carlo!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, Mr. Hartwell! You're looking for tools, you say? How INDUSTRIOUS! I do believe Lord Doily kept a small tool cabinet somewhere behind that tallboy — he was always tinkering with things down here. But I must say, the ventilation appears to be in REASONABLE order — a few cobwebs in the ducts, nothing alarming. Now, I really ought to get back to the LABORATORY and make sure nothing has been disturbed! That machine is in a rather DELICATE state, and I would hate for anyone to injure themselves before I've had a chance to make it safe. If you DO find any tools, do bring them upstairs — I shall need a wrench and perhaps a pair of PLIERS to secure those frayed wires properly!
events.thinking: FRUSTRATION! The vents are too small for any meaningful sabotage — only something tiny could fit through them! My grand secondary-trap ventilation scheme is DASHED! But wait — too small for ME, but perfect for channeling gas or smoke from the laboratory down here! The principle still holds, even if I cannot physically crawl through them! Now — Peter Perfect is rummaging through the furniture looking for tools to fix the machine. This is EXQUISITE! If I help him find tools, he will repair the machine himself, and then I need only make ONE subtle adjustment — a reversed polarity here, a loosened coupling there — and the machine becomes a DEATH TRAP that these buffoons will have built WITH THEIR OWN HANDS! I must stay helpful, stay accommodating, stay SNEEKLY! Back to the laboratory — I need to be there when the 'repairs' happen so I can guide them toward catastrophe!

events.desc: Too small for a man, those vents — but NOT too small for FUMES! If I can rig the laboratory machine to produce a toxic discharge, the ventilation will carry it straight down here into the cellar! But that is the CONTINGENCY plan — the PRIMARY plan remains the machine itself! Peter wants to play HANDYMAN? Oh, let him! Let him fetch his wrench and his pliers and march up to that laboratory feeling like a HERO! Because when Clara Bellingham arrives — and she WILL arrive — these gallant fools will escort her straight to the 'repaired' machine and invite her to pull a lever! And THAT lever will be the one I've subtly reconfigured to deliver a MAGNIFICENT electrical discharge! The beauty of it — they will have BUILT my trap FOR me! Vincent Marsh does not get his hands dirty when he can get VOLUNTEERS! Now — back to the laboratory, before any of these simpletons touches something they shouldn't!

Penelope Pitstop: Well I DO declare! The compartment is opening! Now everyone just HOLD on a moment — Clara Bellingham solved this riddle fair and square, and she intends to see what's inside! A MAP, sugar — the answer was a MAP! Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish! Now let's see what treasures this old mantelpiece has been hiding all these years! Oh, I am just TICKLED pink!
events.thinking: I am BUZZING with excitement! I just solved that riddle and interacted with the mantelpiece — 'cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — it's a MAP, obviously! Now I need to see what that compartment revealed! Dick Dastardly was trying to grab whatever's in there, bless his scheming little heart — though of course I'm SURE he was just being helpful. And that scream he mentioned? Honey, I've been standing right here and I didn't hear a THING. He's probably just confused, poor dear. Let me see what this mantelpiece gave up!

events.desc: Dick tried to tell Danny there was a scream in the Entrance Hall to get everyone to LEAVE. But I didn't hear any scream, and I was standing RIGHT here. Bless his heart, he's probably just excited about the adventure! Now — what did the mantelpiece reveal?

Peter Perfect: Mr Sneekly — with ALL due respect, sir — I asked you about a WRENCH and you have given me a lecture on VENTILATION! I am beginning to wonder if you are being deliberately EVASIVE, but I shall give you the benefit of the doubt because that is what a GENTLEMAN does! In the MEANTIME, I shall conduct my OWN search of this furniture — every drawer, every cabinet, every moth-eaten cushion if I must! A man who can strip a wire but cannot remember where he keeps his TOOLS is either very forgetful or very CUNNING, and I have not yet decided which you are, sir! Now then — let us see what these 'carefully rearranged' pieces are HIDING!
events.thinking: FRUSTRATED! Deeply, thoroughly FRUSTRATED! I asked the man a DIRECT question — where is the wrench? — and he responds by nattering on about VENTILATION and DUST and GEORGIAN FURNITURE! He is DODGING me! Every fibre of my being wants to grab him by the lapels and demand answers, but I am a GENTLEMAN, and gentlemen do not manhandle estate managers, however evasive they may be! But I will NOT be deflected! If Sneekly won't tell me where the tool cabinet is, I shall FIND it myself! That furniture has been 'rearranged with surprising care' — someone has been moving things around down here, and perhaps what they moved is hiding what I need! I shall search every stick of furniture in this cellar until I find that wrench or die trying! Well — not DIE. That would rather defeat the purpose of impressing Clara.

events.desc: Something is WRONG here. Sneekly sends me to the cellar for a wrench, then follows me down and starts inspecting air vents instead of helping me find it? And those vents — 'just big enough for something very small' — what has been crawling through this manor's ventilation? The same something that GNAWED through a wire in the laboratory, perhaps? I am choosing to trust this man, but my trust is wearing THIN! Still — if I find that wrench, I can fix the machine, and THAT will impress Clara far more than standing about being suspicious!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, Mr. Ruffcut! And Sawtooth, my GOODNESS — what a pleasant surprise! I do hope you haven't been touching anything in here? This laboratory is in a rather PRECARIOUS state, I'm afraid. Lord Doily's machine has suffered some damage — a wire gnawed clean through, you see — and I was JUST telling the others I needed to inspect it before anyone gets HURT! Now then, let me have a proper look at this apparatus. As estate manager, it falls to ME to ensure the safety of our guests, and I take that responsibility VERY seriously indeed!
events.thinking: ELATION! Pure, unadulterated ELATION! I am back in my laboratory — MY theatre of operations! But blast it — Rufus Ruffcut and that wretched beaver Sawtooth are HERE! I cannot very well rewire the machine with an audience, can I? No, no — I must be CLEVER about this. First, let me examine the machine closely under the guise of a safety inspection. I need to understand exactly which wire was gnawed through and how I can reconnect it in a way that looks repaired but is actually LETHALLY reconfigured. The workbench has tools but no wrench — perfect, that keeps Peter hunting in the cellar while I work! But these two lumberjacks... I need to either enlist them or dispatch them elsewhere. Perhaps I can use them — the sign says the machine requires THREE operators. Interesting...

events.desc: Oh, this is DELICIOUS! The gnawed wire — probably that wretched beaver's handiwork, ironically — gives me the PERFECT excuse to 'repair' the machine! I shall examine every circuit, every connection, and when I reconnect that wire, I shall route it through the WRONG terminal! A casual observer will see a competent repair — but when the third lever is pulled, instead of powering the gauge, it will send the full electrical charge through the operator's handles! And who will be that third operator? Why, CLARA BELLINGHAM, of course — escorted here by her gallant protectors who think they're helping her solve the treasure hunt! The machine requires THREE operators — I need only ensure Clara is one of them! MAGNIFICENT!

Dick Dastardly: Yes, YES, splendid! The mechanism is clearly a TWO-STAGE affair — very sophisticated, very LORD DOILY! One doesn't simply SAY the answer, one must PRESENT it! And I happen to know — through my EXTENSIVE expertise in Victorian manor security systems — that the key will be hidden among those bookshelves! The upside-down volumes, you see — a CLASSIC cipher arrangement! Now if you'll all just step back and give a PROFESSIONAL room to work...
events.thinking: BLAST! I said the answer — MAP — clear as day, with all the theatrical grandeur of a West End premier, and what happens? NOTHING! No hidden compartment, no secret lever, no shower of diamonds! I feel the hot flush of PUBLIC HUMILIATION creeping up my neck. Everyone SAW me declare the answer with such magnificent confidence, and the mantelpiece just SAT there like a smug stone wall! There must be something MORE to this — perhaps one needs an actual MAP to present to the infernal thing. Those bookshelves... several volumes upside down... that's a CODE if ever I saw one! Or a hiding place! I must search them before that mob of interfering do-gooders beats me to it!

events.desc: Curses! CURSES! The blasted mantelpiece did NOTHING! My moment of triumph turned into a moment of standing there like a lemon in a waistcoat! But Reginald Foxworth does NOT admit defeat — those upside-down books are SCREAMING 'secret compartment' and I intend to find what's hidden before Pitstop or those walking quarries get their mitts on it!
events.thinking: BLAST! I said the answer — MAP — clear as day, with all the theatrical grandeur of a West End premier, and what happens? NOTHING! The Ant Hill Mob: CLARA! Oh THANK GAWD, you're ALIVE! You're 'ERE! You're ACTUALLY 'ERE! I been runnin' through this whole bleedin' manor — up the stairs, down the stairs, through the KITCHEN for cryin' out loud — terrified you'd been kidnapped or WORSE! And you're just sittin' 'ere readin' BOOKS like it's a Sunday afternoon! I could — I could — oh, me 'eart's goin' like a jackhammer, I swear on me nan's grave! Right, NOBODY MOVE! Dum Dum, guard that door! Clinger, guard the OTHER door! Zippy — where IS Zippy? — don't matter, guard SOMEFING! And YOU, Foxworth — step AWAY from that mantelpiece! What are you pullin' out of there, eh?! Booby traps from the Siege of Khartoum, my AUNT FANNY! I ain't clever but I know when someone's nickin' somefing! Let me 'ave a look at what you've — OI, WATCH IT — sorry, sorry, me foot caught on the — WHOOPS!
events.thinking: RELIEF. Pure, overwhelming, STAGGERING relief. She's 'ERE! Clara's RIGHT 'ERE! I been runnin' through this manor like a headless chicken, terrified out of me mind, and she's been sittin' in the LIBRARY the whole time! I could cry — I genuinely could CRY! But wait — wait wait wait — Dastardly's 'ere too, and 'e's got 'is 'ands IN that mantelpiece! 'E told everyone to go to the kitchen and then snuck in 'ere with Clara! And now 'e's pullin' things out of secret compartments! I don't know WHAT 'e's up to but me stomach's doin' somersaults and that ain't just the nerves!

events.desc: I'm so relieved I could faint. But somethin' ain't right about Foxworth. 'E sends everyone to the kitchen, then sneaks in 'ere alone with Clara? And now 'e's rootin' around in secret compartments? I can't work out what 'e's DOIN' exactly — I never can — but I know I need to get between 'im and whatever 'e's found in that fireplace. If I trip over me own feet on the way there... well, that's just 'ow we do things, innit?

They seem the domestic type, in their own terrifying way. I must enlist their aid!

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah — the INSCRIPTION! I do beg your pardon, Mr. Dastardly, but as estate manager I feel I really MUST assist with Lord Doily's riddle before anyone damages the mechanism! You see, his lordship was terribly fond of wordplay, and this particular puzzle is one I've seen referenced in his personal papers! 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — why, it's a MAP, of course! A MAP! Lord Doily would have built the answer INTO the mechanism — one simply needs to speak it or find the corresponding trigger! Allow me — I know how these old mantelpieces are constructed. One wrong move and the whole thing could SEAL itself permanently!
